title: Warp occupancy and memory thrashing audit
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an engineering audit of several recurring microstall patterns we observed across attention kernels (FlashAttention variants, paged attention, and small fused-op kernels). Goal: identify root causes for transient tail-latency spikes that correlate with low warp occupancy and bursts of DRAM traffic ("memory thrashing"), and propose conservative heuristics that runtime routing can use to pick kernel variants at inference time.

Background / Why this matters:
- Customer workloads with heterogeneous sequence lengths and small-batch spikeiness see 5–30% tail-latency regressions depending on model and quantization profile.
- Existing kernel selector currently prefers FlashAttention-v2 for most length ranges due to raw throughput, but we see pathological cases where FlashAttention's internal tiling leads to low SM utilization and large L2/DRAM storms on A100/H100.
- Paged-attention (our hybrid flash-paged path) avoids some memory pressure but incurs higher per-token overhead for short sequences. Fused kernels are great for steady-state medium batches but brittle under cross-request memory oversubscription.

Testbed and tools used:
- HW: Nvidia A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100 (DGX-style instances).
- SW: CUDA 11.8/12.1 runtimes, cuBLAS/cuDNN counters, nvprof/Nsight, perf counters via nsys + custom eviction tracing hooks.
- Harness: microbench harness that simulates real customer request mix (sequence length distribution, small-batch spike generator).
- Metrics captured: median/95/99 latency per kernel, achieved warp occupancy, warp efficiency, SM active cycles, L2 read/write throughput, DRAM BW, PCIe/PCIEe (if staging across host pinned memory), kernel launch overheads.

Representative experiments (summary):
1) Short-seq spike (L=8–16, batch bursts of 1–8, 10k requests/min)
   - FlashAttention-v2: median 3.8ms/token, p99 12.2ms/token, warp occupancy 0.21, L2 read throughput spikes to 1.6x baseline at p99
   - Paged-attn: median 4.5ms/token, p99 7.1ms/token, warp occupancy 0.6, L2 read throughput more stable
   - Fused-op small-batch kernel: median 3.6ms/token, p99 14.5ms/token, observed kernel preemption and scheduler queuing
   Observations: FlashAttention tiling results in uneven lane utilization for tiny sequences; kernel runtime reorganizes reads into larger tile-sized bursts causing transient L2/DRAM spikes.

2) Mixed-length fluid workload (mix: 60% L=64, 30% L=256, 10% L=8; sustained QPS)
   - FlashAttention-v2: overall best throughput, but when short seqs are interleaved, p95 latency increases 18% due to eviction storms.
   - Hybrid-paged fallback: 6% lower peak throughput, but p99 reduced by 22% across the mix.

3) Large-seq long context (L=1024, small batches)
   - Paged-attn becomes beneficial due to reduced memory-reserved working set; FlashAttention still wins on raw throughput if batch sizes > 4.

Root-cause hypotheses and evidence:
- Hypothesis A: Tile-aligned prefetch in flash kernels causes periodic DRAM bursts when request sequences do not align with the tile grid. Evidence: NVPROF/NSYS show periodic L2-Rd bursts synchronized with kernel launches for L < tile_width.
- Hypothesis B: Small-batch fused kernels suffer from scheduler preemption and underutilized warps due to scalar prologue/epilogue overheads dominating short kernels. Evidence: High ratio of prologue cycles to compute cycles at L<16; profiler shows many SMs enter idle spin waiting for memory coalesces.
- Hypothesis C: Memory thrashing arises when multiple kernels choose identical high-throughput but high-L2 working-set footprints; combined working set exceeds L2 and causes repeated DRAM refills. Evidence: When we artificially force alternate kernels (flash/paged) across adjacent streams, L2 misses fall and tail latency improves.

Actionable heuristics (runtime rules to implement):
1) Sequence-length-based soft thresholds: For batch_size<=4 and seq_length<=16, prefer paged-attn or the small fused kernel with prologue-optimized path disabled (i.e., prefer slightly higher median but lower p99).
2) Occupancy-aware switch: If measured recent average warp occupancy < 0.35 for this model+variant, probabilistically route short sequences to paged-attn for the next N requests (N configurable).
3) L2 pressure signal: Expose an L2 miss-rate metric from the GPU agent; if moving-window L2-miss-rate > 0.12, trigger kernel diversity (round-robin between flash and paged) to avoid synchronized working sets.
4) Prefetch distance tuning: Adjust FlashAttention prefetch distance down by 1 for lengths < tile_width to smooth DRAM bursts (empirically reduced p99 by ~18% in short-seq test).

Implementation notes and conservative rollouts:
- Start with a canary on a small subset of serving hosts with additional tracing enabled (JIRA-RT-3245 tracking).
- Implement occupancy and L2-miss-rate as lightweight sampling counters (sample every M requests to avoid overhead).
- Add a self-healing fallback that reverts selector to default static policy if p50/p95 regress beyond a small epsilon for the canary group.

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Impact on multi-tenant nodes: does the round-robin heuristic harm one tenant consistently? Need synthetic multi-tenant matrices.
- Quantized operators (int8/4-bit) behave differently: run same microbench with quantized kernels.
- H100 microarchitecture difference: verify prefetch-distance tuning still helpful or if SM scheduling handles it better.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- PR: add occupancy sampling hook + selector switch (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1428) — assigned to Marco.
- Bench: run multi-tenant matrix (Ethan) — target complete by 2024-11-08.
- Instrumentation: add L2-miss-rate exporter for console dashboards (Lina) — WIP.

Notes to reviewers:
- This audit intentionally errs on the conservative side; we prefer reduced p99 over raw median throughput in customer-facing default policy.
- Please review the proposed thresholds (seq<=16, occupancy<0.35, L2-miss-rate>0.12) — they are empirically tuned on our testbed but likely need smoothing when exposed to production distributions.

Appendix (raw numbers excerpt):
- Short-seq burst, FlashAttention-v2: occupancy=0.21, warp-eff=0.62, L2-rd=320 GB/s (baseline 200 GB/s), DRAM=780 GB/s spike
- Short-seq burst, Paged-attn: occupancy=0.61, warp-eff=0.87, L2-rd=160 GB/s
- Mixed workload, FlashAttention p95: +18% latency vs hybrid selector

End of audit.
